arxiv-1806-00885.title: Elasticizing Linux via Joint Disaggregation of Memory and Computation
arxiv-1806-00885.creator: Ehab Ababneh, Zaid Al-Ali, Sangtae Ha, Richard Han, Eric Keller
arxiv-1806-00885.description: Abstract Abstract In this paper, we propose a set of operating system primitives which provides a scaling abstraction to cloud applications in which they can transparently be enabled to support scaled execution across multiple physical nodes as resource needs go beyond that available on a single machine.

arxiv-2105-05548.title: Modeling space-time trends and dependence in extreme precipitations of Burkina Faso by the approach of the Peaks-Over-Threshold
arxiv-2105-05548.creator: Béwentaoré Sawadogo
arxiv-2105-05548.description: Abstract Abstract. Modeling extremes of climate variables in the framework of climate change is a particularly difficult task, since it implies taking into account spatio-temporal non-stationarities. In this paper, we propose a new method for estimating extreme precipitation at the points where we have not observations using information from marginal distributions and dependence structure.

arxiv-2201-01381.title: Graph Decipher: A transparent dual-attention graph neural network to understand the message-passing mechanism for the node classification Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-2201-01381.creator: Yan Pang, Chao Liu
arxiv-2201-01381.description: Abstract Graph neural networks can be effectively applied to find solutions for many real-world problems across widely diverse fields. The success of graph neural networks is linked to the message-passing mechanism on the graph, however the message-aggregating behavior is still not entirely clear in most algorithms.

arxiv-2207-07749.title: Bootstrap State Representation using Style Transfer for Better Generalization in Deep Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2207-07749.creator: Md Masudur Rahman✉, Yexiang Xue
arxiv-2207-07749.description: Abstract Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents often overfit the training environment, leading to poor generalization performance. In this paper, we propose Thinker, a bootstrapping method to remove adversarial effects of confounding features from the observation in an unsupervised way, and thus, it improves RL agents’ generalization. Thinker first clusters experience trajectories into several clusters.

arxiv-2209-03116.title: A New Method for the High-Precision Assessment of Tumor Changes in Response to Treatment.
arxiv-2209-03116.creator: Paul Tar, Neil Thacker, J.P.B. O’Connor et. al.
arxiv-2209-03116.description: Abstract Tina Memo No. 2018-004 Green Open Access pre-print of publication in Bioinformatics 2018 Mar 14. doi: 10.1093. See also 2017-006 and 2015-014. abstract Motivation: Imaging demonstrates that preclinical and human tumors are heterogeneous, i.e. a single tumor can exhibit multiple regions that behave differently during both normal development and also in response to treatment.

arxiv-2210-00177.title: Deterministic Laser Writing of Spin Defects in Nanophotonic Cavities
arxiv-2210-00177.creator: Aaron M. Day, Jonathan R. Dietz, Madison Sutula, Matthew Yeh, Evelyn L. Hu
arxiv-2210-00177.description: Abstract High-yield engineering and characterization of cavity-emitter coupling is an outstanding challenge in developing scalable quantum network nodes. Ex-situ defect formation processes prevent real-time defect-cavity characterization, and previous in-situ methods require further processing to improve emitter properties or are limited to bulk substrates. We demonstrate direct laser-writing of cavity-integrated spin defects using a nanosecond-pulsed above-bandgap laser.

arxiv-2210-10486.title: Cross-Modal Fusion Distillation for Fine-Grained Sketch-Based Image Retrieval
arxiv-2210-10486.creator: Abhra Chaudhuri, Massimiliano Mancini 2 ​ Yanbei Chen 2 ​ Zeynep Akata 2,3,4 ​ Anjan Dutta \text{Massimiliano Mancini}^{\text{2}}\\ \text{Yanbei Chen}^{\text{2}}\\ \text{Zeynep Akata}^{\text{2,3,4}}\\ \text{Anjan Dutta}
arxiv-2210-10486.description: Abstract Representation learning for sketch-based image retrieval has mostly been tackled by learning embeddings that discard modality-specific information. As instances from different modalities can often provide complementary information describing the underlying concept, we propose a cross-attention framework for Vision Transformers (XModalViT) that fuses modality-specific information instead of discarding them.

arxiv-2211-12658.title: Asymptotics of Discrete q q -Freud II \mathrm{II} orthogonal polynomials from the q q -Riemann Hilbert Problem
arxiv-2211-12658.creator: Nalini Joshi 1, Tomas Lasic Latimer 2
arxiv-2211-12658.description: Abstract . We investigate a Riemann-Hilbert problem (RHP), whose solution corresponds to a group of q q -orthogonal polynomials studied earlier by Ismail et al . Using RHP theory we determine new asymptotic results in the limit as the degree of the polynomials approach infinity. The RHP formulation also enables us to obtain further properties.

arxiv-2308-04328.title: The Product Beyond the Model – An Empirical Study of Repositories of Open-Source ML Products
arxiv-2308-04328.creator: Nadia Nahar 1 2 , Haoran Zhang 2 , Grace Lewis 3 , Shurui Zhou 4 , Christian Kästner 2
arxiv-2308-04328.description: Abstract Machine learning (ML) components are increasingly incorporated into software products for end-users, but developers face challenges in transitioning from ML prototypes to products. Academics have limited access to the source of commercial ML products, hindering research progress to address these challenges.

arxiv-2511-05550.title: Factual and Musical Evaluation Metrics for Music Language Models
arxiv-2511-05550.creator: Daniel Chenyu Lin, Michael Freeman, John Thickstun
arxiv-2511-05550.description: Abstract Music language models (Music LMs), like vision language models, leverage multimodal representations to answer natural language queries about musical audio recordings. Although Music LMs are reportedly improving, we find that current evaluations fail to capture whether their answers are correct.

pmc-10599010.title: Association between Yili goose sperm motility and expression profiles of mRNA and miRNA in testis
pmc-10599010.creator: Yingping Wu, Lihua Zhang, Haiying Li, Xiaoyu Zhao, Yawen Ding, Yingying Yao, Ling Wang
pmc-10599010.description: BackgroundThe study was conducted to find out the candidate microRNA (miRNA) and genes that associated with sperm motility of Yili goose through small RNA sequencing of testicular tissue of Yili goose, and provide a theoretical basis for the study of the regulation mechanism of sperm motility of Yili goose gander.

pmc-10675211.title: Mycotoxin Occurrence in Milk and Durum Wheat Samples from Tunisia Using Dispersive Liquid–Liquid Microextraction and Liquid Chromatography with Fluorescence Detection
pmc-10675211.creator: Khouloud Ben Hassouna, Ahmed M Hamed, Jalila Ben Salah-Abbès, Kamel Chaieb, Samir Abbès, Ana M García-Campaña, Laura Gámiz-Gracia
pmc-10675211.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Food and feed contamination with mycotoxins is a major public health concern. Humans and animals are exposed to these toxins by consuming contaminated products throughout their lives. In this study, a method based on dispersive liquid–liquid microextraction (DLLME), followed by liquid chromatography with fluorescence detection (LC-FLD), was validated for the determination of aflatoxins (AFs) M1, B1, B2, G1, G2, zearalenone (ZEN), and ochratoxin A (OTA).

pmc-12817871.title: AND logic-gated CRISPR/Cas9 and hybridization chain reaction system for precise ctDNA detection
pmc-12817871.creator: Tianliang Ji, Yujia Zhang, Yixiu Wang, Kaiyu Yuan, Mingxiang Wang, Jingyi Ye, Honglu Zhang, Ning Zhang, Huan Zhang
pmc-12817871.description: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is a critical biomarker for liquid biopsies, enabling the non-invasive acquisition of cancer-related information from blood samples. Precise detection of ctDNA, particularly the identification of single-nucleotide variations (SNVs), is crucial for early cancer diagnosis, therapeutic monitoring, and prognostic evaluation.

pmc-13454286.creator: Ahmad Shafee, Kavikumar Jacob, Naveed Iqbal, Ahmed A Hamoud
pmc-13454286.description: The Zika virus is a relatively new pathogen that has quickly become a major issue in virology. Infectious mosquitoes of the Aedes genus, particularly Aedes aegypti, spread the Zika virus in tropical and subtropical areas. Most bites from Aedes mosquitoes occur during the daytime. Dengue, chikungunya, and urban yellow fever are all spread by the same insects.
